subject: Optimization of runtime with virtual machine

messages.author: 4076f5688b45a1a5
messages.subject: Optimization of runtime with virtual machine
parts:
Good morning,
I have a quick question for you. I have recently gained access to a virtual machine to run an INLA model with a huge dataset (spatial data during one year).  
I had to ask for the VM because the excessive memory needed made my PC crash.
That problem is solved, but now I wonder if there is a way to speed up the running (it took 55 minutes just to get through the first complete global iteration). 
I used the same code as I did locally, but maybe there is something I can do to exploit the 24 cpus in a better way.
Thank you, 
Alessandro

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Optimization of runtime with virtual machine
parts:
I would guess so. I presume you have Linux on the VM, then register for
the PARDISO library, with

inla.pardiso()

its all there already, you just need to activate it.

make sure you have R-4.2 and the most recent testing version

if H is the number of hyperparametes, then set

num.threads="A:B"

where A=2*H+1 or 2*H, and B=1 or 2

if its still slow, send data/code so i can recheck here

Best
H
